title: Choose Anchorflow's visual world
question: Anchorflow pins GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and audits the workflow, all in the browser. The roll assigned Certified Copy. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Certified Copy
options.lineage: Notarial certificates and security printing: guilloché rosettes, intaglio green, numbered serials
options.thesis: Every pin is a certified entry: the result reads as a certified copy of your workflow, and each pinned action carries a seal drawn from its own commit SHA, so the same SHA always draws the same seal and a changed one is visible at a glance.
options.viewport: Header: rosette mark + Anchorflow, nav (Pin · Compare · Guide · FAQ), theme, Nor AI mark. H1 'Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, in your browser'. Left 40%: your workflow editor. Right 60%: the certified copy. A one-line verdict ('4 of 8 actions ride moving tags · 1 critical injection · 3 over-broad grants'), the primary 'Resolve & pin 4 refs' with its network disclosure, then the uses ledger where pinned lines wear their seal + short SHA. Findings, token grants, diff and receipts sit as tabs beneath.
options.risk: Guilloché used as wallpaper turns into a banknote costume; it must stay on the seals and one header rule. The certificate metaphor also has to stay subordinate to a clean working screen.

raised.raise: Datamatics density: every SHA is shown in full 40-hex tabular mono where it matters (ledger, receipts), never ellipsised to look tidy.
Star-atlas magnitude ramp: severity is carried by mark size on one fixed ramp as well as by colour and a word, so nothing depends on colour alone.
J-card hard halves: on phones the result flips between 'As pasted' and 'Pinned' as two whole sides instead of a cramped side-by-side diff.
Feed focus: one next step owns the verdict line at a time (paste → resolve → copy), re-written after each step.

options.label: Manifest & Bolt Seals
options.lineage: Customs cargo manifests and numbered tamper-evident bolt seals
options.thesis: Your workflow is a cargo manifest. Every action is a container, and pinning snaps a numbered bolt seal (the short SHA) on it; a moving tag is an unsealed container, and the receipt is the manifest line a customs officer can re-check.
options.viewport: Navy band header with stencil 'Anchorflow' and nav. H1 on the band. Below: editor left, manifest right: rows of actions with an orange bolt-seal tag (sealed: short SHA; open: 'unsealed · @v4'). 'Seal 4 containers' primary. Findings and grants as tabs.
options.risk: Familiar: shipping/containers is the metaphor half the DevOps world already uses (Docker), so it reads less distinct. Stencil type can tip into industrial costume.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.lineage: International airport sign systems: yellow overhead bands, black humanist sans, monumental gate numbers
options.thesis: Hardening a workflow is a connection to make: a sticky yellow band always shows the one next decision with its count at gate-number scale, and re-signs itself after each step.
options.viewport: A full-width yellow band under the header: '4 → Resolve moving tags · 4 read-only requests to api.github.com'. Below it a white work area: editor left, result right with the uses list. The band re-signs to '→ Copy pinned file' after resolving.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins product clarity (it is literally a guided flow, the fix for the cockpit), but engineers don't identify with airport signage, and the yellow band shouts on a tool used daily.
options.risk: Loud on repeat use; yellow + black reads 'warning' to security engineers.

options.label: Dark-first Developer Console
options.lineage: Graphite developer consoles with syntax-derived accents and hairline seams
options.thesis: Anchorflow as a native piece of the developer's dark editor: graphite panels, syntax-coloured state, hairline seams.
options.viewport: Graphite shell, editor left with syntax highlighting, result panel right with collapsible sections.
options.case: Engineers identify with it instantly, but it is closest to the cockpit the redesign is meant to remove and to every other dev tool.
options.risk: Indistinct; the owner's 'cockpit-like workspace' complaint lives here.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.case: Pure black and white cannot say critical vs pinned vs moving; loses clarity, and audience identification is aesthetic only.
options.kept: Density courage: full 40-hex SHAs in tabular mono, never ellipsised.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: A workflow is not a sky; jobs as constellations obscures line numbers and order.
options.kept: One fixed magnitude ramp: severity also encoded by mark size.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.case: Handwriting undermines exactness; no audience link.
options.kept: Hard halves: As pasted / Pinned as two whole sides on phones.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: One finding per screen hides the file; engineers need the whole workflow in view.
options.kept: One next step owns the verdict line at a time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean GitHub-style light tool: white ground, Primer-like blue accent, two panes and tabs, the way hosted hardening services look, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Header, H1, editor left, tabbed result right (Pinned · Findings · Permissions · Diff).
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the hosted competitors by design.
